library(stringr)

```{r}
# ====================================================================
# STEP 0: Load the Data
# ====================================================================
# Load the dataset exactly as you saved it from Phase 1
stars1 <- readRDS("stars_cleaned_eda.rds")

# ====================================================================
# STEP 1: PRE-PROCESS (LOCF on Long Data)
# ====================================================================
stars1_locf <- stars1 %>%
  # 1a. Sort chronologically for each student
  arrange(student_id, grade) %>%
  group_by(student_id) %>%
  # 1b. Safely fill fixed demographic traits backwards and forwards ACROSS ROWS
  fill(student_gender, student_race, birth_year, birth_month, .direction = "downup") %>%
  ungroup()

# ====================================================================
# STEP 2: PIVOT TO WIDE FORMAT (For MICE and Causal Inference)
# ====================================================================
stars1_wide <- stars1_locf %>%
  # 2a. Select only what we need
  select(
    student_id, grade, 
    student_gender, student_race,                  # Constants
    math_score, class_type, free_lunch, area_type, # Time-variant confounders/treatments
    treads, wordsk                                 # Time-variant auxiliary predictors
  ) %>%
  # 2b. Pivot time-variant columns into grade-specific columns
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = grade,
    values_from = c(math_score, class_type, free_lunch, area_type, treads, wordsk),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{grade}"
  ) %>%
  # 2c. Create the critical target variable for the Doubly Robust missingness model
  mutate(stayed_g3 = as.numeric(!is.na(math_score_3))) %>%
  # 2d. Factorize everything so MICE knows what to do
  mutate(across(c(student_gender, student_race, starts_with("class_type"), 
                  starts_with("free_lunch"), starts_with("area_type")), as.factor))

# Quick sanity check
cat("Dimensions of Wide Data (Should equal total number of unique students):\n")
dim(stars1_wide)
```

```{r}
# ====================================================================
# STEP 3: MICE Imputation (Imputing Z and A)
# ====================================================================
# We MUST drop student_id from the imputation process, otherwise MICE 
# will try to use the student's ID number as a numeric predictor, 
# which will ruin the math and take forever to run.

stars_mice_input <- stars1_wide %>% select(-student_id)

cat("Running MICE Engine... (This will take a moment with 27 columns)\n")
set.seed(2026207)
# m = 5 imputations. printFlag = FALSE keeps your console clean.
imp_data <- mice(stars_mice_input, m = 20, maxit = 20, printFlag = FALSE)


# ====================================================================
# STEP 4: The MID Maneuver (Imputation then Deletion)
# ====================================================================
# Extract the long format of the imputed data (includes .imp == 0, the original data)
long_data <- complete(imp_data, action = "long", include = TRUE)

# The Deletion Step: Group by the unique row ID (.id) and force the imputed 
# math_score_3 to perfectly match the original original data (.imp == 0)
long_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(.id) %>%
  mutate(math_score_3 = math_score_3[.imp == 0]) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Convert back to a MICE 'mids' object so the causal packages can read it
imp_data_mid <- as.mids(long_data)

# Sanity Check
cat("\nMID Complete! Checking missingness in Imputed Dataset #1:\n")
cat("math_score_3 NAs (Should be thousands, representing dropouts): ", 
    sum(is.na(complete(imp_data_mid, 1)$math_score_3)), "\n")
cat("free_lunch_K NAs (Should be 0, fully imputed): ", 
    sum(is.na(complete(imp_data_mid, 1)$free_lunch_K)), "\n")
```
